portraits.name: Rolf
portraits.prompt: Use case: stylized-concept. Create ONE original square fantasy RPG NPC portrait of Rolf. The attached image is a rendering-style reference ONLY, not an edit target: match its crisp square pixel clusters, controlled color ramps, black background, integrated chest-up anatomy and readable face. Do not copy its identity, armor or costume. Output square PNG at 1254 x 1254 if possible. Sophisticated pixel art with approximately 176x176 logical detail enlarged with hard edges, no blur, no photorealism, no smooth painterly gradients. Subject: human young adult man in his early twenties, clean-shaven, short tousled blond hair, friendly expression. Plain red shirt and blue cloth bib apron, both clearly visible. Chest-up composition facing nearly forward so both eyes and scarred cheek are clear, pure black background, no props, no text, no border. CRITICAL SCARS: Exactly TWO healed parallel diagonal scars on the VIEWER'S LEFT side of the face (the man's anatomical right). Outer longer scar extends from just ABOVE the eye on the viewer's left, across the brow area, down to the MIDDLE of that cheek. Inner shorter parallel scar is closer to the nose and upper lip on the SAME viewer-left side, extending beside the nose toward the upper lip. Both scars slant in the same direction and are separated clearly. Eye intact and open. The other side of the face is unscarred. Natural warm skin, expressive friendly face, practical simple clothing. Face readable at 88x88. Independently composed original character.
portraits.revision_prompt: Edit this Rolf portrait only to correct scars. Preserve face, friendly expression, hair, clothing, framing, pixel art style and black background. There are currently THREE separate diagonal scar lines on viewer's left. Replace them with EXACTLY TWO parallel scars: one long continuous scar from just above the viewer-left eye through the outer brow region to mid cheek, and one shorter parallel scar beside the nose ending near the upper lip. Remove the extra third scar completely, healing that skin. The long scar should be a single continuous line, not separated into two offset lines. Both scars slope from upper right toward lower left as seen by viewer. Eye remains intact. No scars on viewer's right. Preserve everything else.
